$comment: Lighthouse CI budgets (issue #32). docs/seo.md §12 recorded this as NOT BUILT,
on the grounds that per-route budgets need a measured baseline that did not
exist — and that 'a budget nobody can pass gets disabled within a week, which
is worse than no budget'. That reasoning is why the numbers below are split
into two kinds rather than set uniformly.
MEASURED, THEREFORE ENFORCED: accessibility, best-practices and SEO are all
100 on all five routes, measured 2026-09-19 against a production build over
three runs each (medians):
/                        perf  94   a11y 100   bp 100   seo 100
/cv                      perf  99   a11y 100   bp 100   seo 100
/about                   perf  91   a11y 100   bp 100   seo 100
/projects/1              perf  94   a11y 100   bp 100   seo 100
/notes/discoverability   perf 100   a11y 100   bp 100   seo 100
The three enforced categories are deterministic — they inspect the DOM and
the response, not the clock — so a CI runner under load returns the same
score as a laptop. A regression in one is a real defect, so these fail the
build.
Three fixes were needed to make 100 reachable rather than aspirational, and
all three were real defects rather than concessions to the tooling:

1. The footer's split-flap text carried `aria-label` on /

, where
ARIA prohibits it — capping accessibility at 96 on EVERY page, since
the footer is site-wide.
2. The project pages requested three background textures that have never
existed in this repository, so every view logged three 404s.
3. Vercel's two telemetry scripts 404 anywhere but Vercel, which is every
CI run. The root layout now mounts them only when VERCEL is set.
A fourth was caught and reverted rather than fixed: /notes/[slug] shipped
without the shared backdrop, and the PageTitle subtitle then composited
against the bare body colour at 2.9:1 — just under the 3:1 floor for large
text. Restoring the backdrop restored both the score and the consistency.
NOT YET MEASURED IN CI, THEREFORE WARNED: performance. It is timing-dependent
and a shared GitHub runner is both slower and far noisier than any developer
machine, so a threshold picked from local numbers would fail on green builds.
It is collected and reported on every run; once a few weeks of CI numbers
exist, the floor can be set from THEM and promoted to an error. Until then a
warning is honest and a hard failure would be theatre.

$comment-url: Five routes, chosen to cover the distinct rendering shapes rather than to
be exhaustive: the homepage (the WebGL hero and the orbital nav), /cv (a
pure static document with no client JS of its own), /about (the heaviest
page — live GitHub telemetry and the most client components), one project
detail page (the three.js scene behind a dynamic boundary) and one note
(the longest single document on the site, ~240KB of generated HTML — the
only page whose weight comes from prose rather than from scripts).
Adding every route would multiply the runtime to re-measure the same
$comment-runs: Three runs, median reported. A single run on a shared runner is noisy
enough that an unlucky one would fail an otherwise green build — the
exact 'cries wolf' failure the deleted-then-ignored budget was about.

$comment-preset: Desktop, matching the device the baseline above was measured on. Mobile
throttling would be the more demanding target and is the right one to
add LATER, as a second collect block, once the desktop numbers have a
CI history. Changing the preset now would invalidate the baseline in
the same commit that introduces it.
$comment-skip: uses-http2 is decided by Vercel's edge, not by anything in this
repository, and always fails against a local `next start`.
`canonical` is deliberately NOT skipped, although the obvious
prediction is that it would fail: every page served from localhost
declares a canonical on https://ma.codes. It was measured instead of
assumed, and it passes — Lighthouse reports a cross-origin canonical
rather than failing one. Skipping it would have dropped a real SEO
audit to avoid a problem that does not exist.
`errors-in-console` is also NOT skipped, for a stronger reason: it
used to fail off-platform because Vercel's two telemetry scripts 404
anywhere but Vercel. That was fixed at the source — the root layout
only mounts them when `process.env.VERCEL` is set — rather than by
silencing the audit, which would have hidden every real console error
along with the two fake ones.

$comment-upload: Filesystem, not temporary-public-storage. The reports are uploaded as a
workflow artifact instead, which keeps them inside the repository's own
access controls — `temporary-public-storage` publishes a full report,
including every request URL, to a public bucket.
